issue.title: @angular/common/http HttpClient .jsonp does not support options or headers
issue.body:
## I'm submitting a... 

[x] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[ ] Bug report  
[ ] Performance issue
[ ] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
[ ] Other... Please describe:
## Current behavior Certain sites require that HTTP headers be provided when making a JSONP request. `@angular/http` used to allow this functionality, but the non-deprecated `@angular/common/http` no longer allows any options/headers to be provided to the `.jsonp(url, callback)` call. ## Expected behavior `.jsonp(url, callback)` on `HttpClient` from `@angular/common/http` should allow options/headers to be provided. In particular I am attempting to provide the `Accept: application/json' header for an API integration. All other HttpClient methods (get/post/etc.) support options and HttpHeaders. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions ```javascript import { Injectable } from '@angular/core'; import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'; @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) export class TestService { constructor(private http: HttpClient) { } public query(search: string): any { this.http.post(`https://someUrl`, 'someCallback').subscribe((response) => { console.log(response); }); } } ``` ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? There are some services that can provide both `application/xml` and `application/json` responses. The `Accept` header is required to choose the desired response format. Also, the `Cookie` header is required to maintain authentication to some APIs. ## Environment 

Angular version: 6.0.3

- Platform: Windows 10

body: Looking at the more contemporary `JsonpClientBackend`, it seems like this would still be an issue. For anyone interested in sending a PR, take a look at `JsonpClientBackend` as the code location for a fix.
